# The 10 AI regulatory dates to watch through 2027

Source: https://lowob.com/research/the-10-ai-regulatory-dates-to-watch-through-2027/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-22 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Strategy

> Summary: The AI-specific rules keep slipping. The record-keeping, supervision and resilience rules that already apply do not. Most of what binds a bank's AI in 2027 is old law, newly read to cover agents. This list, refreshed on 16 November 2026, sets out the ten dates that change what a financial firm in the US, UK or EU must do or show, and what happened to the dates that have passed since it was first published.

## Key points

- Two new EU AI Act prohibitions and the machine-readable marking duty for generative output apply from 2 December 2026.
- Colorado's replacement AI law, signed on 14 May 2026, takes effect on 1 January 2027 with notice, adverse-outcome explanation and human review duties.
- The US banking agencies' promised request for information on generative and agentic AI had not appeared by late October 2026.
- EU AI Act Annex III high-risk obligations, including credit scoring of individuals, apply from 2 December 2027.
- The ECB's end-October 2026 deadline for AI cyber-threat plans has passed; supervisors are now asking whether banks can audit and stop their agents.

This list is for heads of AI, risk and compliance at financial firms operating in the US, UK or EU. Skip it if your AI use is limited to drafting internal documents with no customer impact.

## How we chose

We kept dates that change what a financial firm must do or show, in the order they arrive, and left out consultations with no deadline attached. Every date is from a regulator, a court record, a law firm's reading of the text or a named press report, cited below. Where a date is not fixed, we say so rather than guess.

## What happened since October

Three items from the first version of this list, or close to it, have now passed.

**End of October 2026: ECB AI cyber-threat plans.** According to Reuters, the ECB gave euro zone lenders until the end of October to produce plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats, including better back-up and recovery. Banks were also asked to map how AI is used across their businesses and third-party providers, and to make sure they could switch systems off and restart them in a controlled way. Reuters reported on 13 October that some firms still had significant gaps. The ECB has not published a read-out of the submissions. DORA, which has applied since 17 January 2025, remains the legal frame for that work.

**19 October 2026: the FCA's AI good practice review.** The FCA published *AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement*. It sets no new rules, but it names the records it expects: prompts, outputs, model versions, applied filters and escalation decisions, and auditable decisions with rationale and challenge. It also flags firms whose AI decisions were "poorly documented with limited audit trails."

**14 October 2026: the first harmonised standard.** The Commission published EN 18286, a quality management system standard, under the AI Act. Following it gives providers a presumption of conformity for the requirements it covers. It does not yet cover logging, which remains in the standardisation pipeline.

## The list

| # | When | What happens | Who it affects | What to do now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2 December 2026 | Two new EU AI Act prohibitions apply: systems that generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery. Machine-readable marking of synthetic output under Article 50(2) also applies to generative systems already on the market | Any firm offering generative AI in the EU | Confirm your vendors mark synthetic output and that your own builds do too |
| 2 | December 2026 (expected) | FINRA's 2027 oversight report, if it follows the 2026 report's release on 9 December 2025 | US broker-dealers | Re-read the 2026 report's agent section and check you can track agent actions and decisions |
| 3 | 1 January 2027 | Colorado's Automated Decision-Making Technology in Consequential Decisions Act takes effect, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act: notice before use, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, and meaningful human review on request | Developers and deployers using automated decisions in lending, insurance, employment and other covered areas for Colorado consumers | Identify which automated decisions reach Colorado consumers; deployers keep compliance records for three years after each use |
| 4 | Q1 2027 | The FCA publishes its evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort: Aereve, Barclays, Coadjute, Experian, GoCardless, Lloyds Banking Group (Scottish Widows), Palindrome and UBS. Testing ends by the end of 2026 | UK firms | Read it for the supervisor's view of production AI in banking, payments and credit data |
| 5 | Not yet dated | The US banking agencies' request for information on model risk and "banks' use of AI, including generative AI and agentic AI", promised in April when SR 26-2 left both out of scope. Not in the Federal Register as of 24 October 2026 | US banks | Prepare your answer now: how you validate retrieval, guardrails and agent actions, and how you would stop an agent |
| 6 | Not yet dated | A ruling on OpenAI's and Microsoft's summary judgment motions in the news publishers' copyright cases, including *New York Times v. OpenAI*. The publishers filed their opposition in October 2026; no ruling date has been set | Anyone training or fine-tuning on third-party content | Inventory the provenance of every corpus your models touch |
| 7 | Not yet dated | The first lawsuit brought in the name of the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, created under the executive order of 11 December 2025. The DOJ intervened on 24 April 2026 in xAI's challenge to the 2024 Colorado AI Act, which Colorado then repealed and replaced | Firms planning around state AI laws | Avoid building compliance around any single state regime until this settles |
| 8 | 2 August 2027 | General-purpose AI models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 must comply; each member state must have at least one operational AI regulatory sandbox | Model providers directly; firms that fine-tune or rebrand models | Ask your model vendors for their compliance position and documentation |
| 9 | 2 December 2027 | EU AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply, including creditworthiness and credit scoring of individuals, life and health insurance pricing, and recruitment | Lenders, insurers and employers using AI in the EU | Start conformity and logging work now; deployers must keep logs for at least six months |
| 10 | 2 August 2028 | High-risk obligations for AI built into products regulated under Annex I apply | Product makers, rarely financial firms | Note it; little action for most financial firms |

Three items deserve a closer reading.

**Colorado is the US date with teeth.** The original Colorado AI Act was due to take effect on 30 June 2026. The replacement law signed on 14 May 2026 narrows the focus to automated decision-making in consequential decisions, keeps enforcement with the state Attorney General under consumer protection law, and has no private right of action. Its three-year record duty for deployers is a reconstruction requirement in all but name.

**The US bank RFI is late, but the questions are not.** SR 26-2 placed generative and agentic AI outside its scope in April. Reuters reported on 13 October that the Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC were nonetheless asking banks whether agent decisions can be tracked and audited, who approves agent actions, and how a bank would shut autonomous systems down. Firms that wait for the RFI to define expectations will meet them first in an examination.

**The EU high-risk date moved; the logging duty did not change.** Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, moved Annex III obligations to 2 December 2027. Articles 12, 19 and 26, which require automatic logs and their retention, carry no amendment markers in the Commission's consolidated text. Our guide [Regulators want the chain, not the model](https://lowob.com/research/regulators-want-the-chain-not-the-model/) maps those duties against US and UK rules.

> Every date on this list asks the same question in a different accent: show us what the system saw, what it did and who checked.

## What already applies, and is easy to forget

**EU transparency duties.** Most Article 50 duties for chatbots and deepfakes have applied since 2 August 2026. The delay that grabbed headlines covered high-risk systems, not these. Our explainer [The EU AI Act for commercial teams](https://lowob.com/research/the-eu-ai-act-for-commercial-teams/) covers the disclosure duties.

**US supervision and records.** FINRA's rules are technologically neutral, and its 2026 report lists tracking agent actions and decisions and keeping prompt and output logs among firms' considerations. FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4 set retention of three to six years.

**UK accountability.** The FCA says it does not plan AI-specific rules. Its October review places AI inside the Consumer Duty, senior manager accountability, operational resilience and outsourcing rules that already apply.

## Left out, and why

**SEC predictive data analytics rule.** The SEC formally withdrew the proposal on 12 June 2025, with 13 other proposals.

**ISO/IEC 42001 certification.** Voluntary, and it does not give presumption of conformity under the AI Act. Our comparison [NIST AI RMF vs ISO/IEC 42001](https://lowob.com/research/nist-ai-rmf-vs-iso-42001/) explains where it helps.

## The one thing to build regardless

Every date above points to the same artefact: a record you can reconstruct, showing what an AI system saw, what it produced, who checked it, and what was done. Colorado asks deployers to keep it for three years. The AI Act asks for logs. FINRA asks how firms track agent actions. US bank supervisors ask whether agent decisions can be audited. Build that record once and most of this calendar becomes paperwork rather than a project. Our explainer [What is an AI audit trail?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-audit-trail/) sets out the fields.

## lowob takeaways

- **2 December 2026 is the next EU date.** New prohibitions and machine-readable marking of synthetic output.
- **Colorado applies from 1 January 2027.** Notice, adverse-outcome explanation, human review and three-year records.
- **Annex III high-risk applies from 2 December 2027.** Credit scoring and life and health insurance pricing are in scope.
- **Build the reconstructable record.** It answers every date on the list.

## Common questions

### When do EU AI Act high-risk rules apply to credit scoring?

After the Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, high-risk obligations for Annex III systems, including creditworthiness and credit scoring of individuals, apply from 2 December 2027.

### When does Colorado's AI law take effect?

Colorado repealed its 2024 AI Act and replaced it with a law on automated decision-making in consequential decisions, signed on 14 May 2026. It takes effect on 1 January 2027.

### What changes in the EU AI Act on 2 December 2026?

Bans on AI systems that generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery apply, and generative systems already on the market must mark synthetic output in a machine-readable format.

### Have US bank regulators issued AI guidance for generative and agentic AI?

Not yet. SR 26-2 excludes generative and agentic AI, and the promised request for information had not been published by late October 2026, though supervisors are asking banks about agent audit trails and shutdown.
